title: Russia and Ukraine agree large prisoner swap in Abu Dhabi; US envoys then see Putin
dek: Two days of US-mediated talks produced no deal on territory. The Kremlin called its meeting with Witkoff and Kushner useful and said Putin would take up Ukraine with Trump at APEC.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed in Abu Dhabi on a large new exchange of prisoners of war, but two days of US-mediated talks that ended on Wednesday produced no breakthrough on territory, the issue that divides the two sides most. On Thursday the US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner flew to Moscow and met President Vladimir Putin.

Russia's chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, said the sides "have agreed in principle on a new large-scale prisoner exchange", with details to follow, according to reports. David Arakhamia of Ukraine's delegation said it could be one of the largest so far. Mr Kushner said the numbers would be finalised on Thursday; no final figure had been announced by Friday morning. A Russian general staff official told state television the swap could take place within two or three weeks, according to reports.

## Where the sides stand

The talks were the first three-way round since February. Mr Kushner called them "a very tough meeting but a productive one", according to reports, and said territory was the hardest question, with "progress" on a framework for security after the war. "The reality is, is there's no trust right now between the sides," he said.

Mr Medinsky said "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia", restating Moscow's claim to Ukrainian territory, and that the sides had reached understanding on some security questions but not others. Rustem Umerov, who led Ukraine's delegation, spoke of "huge progress" on security issues without giving details, according to reports.

President Volodymyr Zelensky, speaking in Dublin, called the prisoner deal a positive step but said Ukraine would not give up territory. "Ending this war without Europe's participation would be unjust, and it would be impossible," he said. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said European representatives could eventually join but that their statements did not suggest a wish to help the peace process.

Moscow demands all of the Donbas region, which Kyiv rejects, and has pressed for buffer zones and limits on NATO.

## The Moscow meeting

After Thursday's meeting with Mr Putin, his foreign-policy aide Yuri Ushakov said the talks were useful and that Russia had told the envoys NATO "could not expand further", according to reports. He said Mr Putin would continue discussing Ukraine with President Donald Trump at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, on 18-19 November. Mr Witkoff said a new round of three-way talks had been agreed, with Europeans to join, according to a Russian agency. Mr Putin also proposed a joint humanitarian mission to the front-line town of Kostiantynivka.

The fighting has not paused. Russia's defence ministry said it shot down 627 Ukrainian drones overnight into Wednesday, and Ukraine has reported repeated Russian missile and drone attacks on its cities in recent weeks. Neither side's figures can be independently verified.

## Why it matters for India

India buys large volumes of Russian crude and has called repeatedly for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war. Any settlement that eases sanctions on Russia, or any collapse of talks that tightens them, would affect the price and availability of Russian oil for Indian refiners at a time when the Gulf conflict has already pushed crude prices up sharply.

## What happens next

The prisoner exchange is expected within weeks once numbers are agreed. The next three-way round has no date yet. Trump and Putin are due to meet at APEC in Shenzhen.
